slides.notes: Research progress briefing. Build date is rendered dynamically in America/New_York. The scientific evidence date is 27 November 2026. slides.title: A transition-state ensemble will guide Nyl12 redesign
slides.notes: The design objective is to create qualified transition-state (TS) templates from the WT mechanism, then use them to guide sequence design. LigandMPNN proposes sequences around constrained templates; Boltz-2 ranks structural compatibility; OpenMM evaluates matched molecular-dynamics behavior. TS means transition state. The engineering pipeline can be commissioned by 30 November, while nomination requires qualified WT templates and existing scientific gates.

slides.title: Cleavage exposes the catalytic Thr233 N terminus
slides.notes: The mature enzyme is an autocleaved N-terminal nucleophile hydrolase. The α chain comprises residues 1–232 and the β chain starts at Thr233 (residues 233–328). Autocleavage exposes Thr233 at the β-chain N terminus. The Thr233 side-chain hydroxyl initiates acylation; the newly exposed α-amino group is a candidate proton acceptor in a relay hypothesis. Phe113 and Asn186 form oxyanion-hole contacts in the modeled active site. Water-mediated deacylation regenerates the enzyme and releases the carboxyl product; the current pathway campaign focuses on acylation, and hydration/deacylation has not established complete hydrolysis. Exact intersubunit mapping: occupied A/E site ligandI borders chainD95–103 (minimum heavy-atom distance3.623Å) and chainF289–300 (2.768Å); same-unit loops are distant25/31Å. DeepblueD95–103 and orange-redF289–300 identify design priorities, not already-run deletions. Existing oldCIF masks are not clean95–103+tail masks;3_loops/x125 omits95–104,115–121,151–164 and retains289–300. Inputs contain PEG/PGE/water, not PA6. Map author chains explicitly and preserve full-length query.
slides.caption: Thr233 starts the β chain; adjacent subunits border the occupied A/E pocket.

slides.title: The NylC proposal motivates explicit protonation tests

cards.title: Interpretation
cards.text: Motivates testing; assigns no pKa population.

slides.notes: Negoro et al. (2023) motivates evaluating the Asp pair, but the reported NylC mechanistic proposal does not assign a protonation state to mature Nyl12. Mapping is Asp306→Asp272, Asp308→Asp274, Thr267→Thr233. Precursor structures vary in mutations and cleavage state, confounding maturation comparisons. The mature Nyl12 active-site environment is not identical to the NylC precursor site. The early Nyl12 ASH272 hypothesis followed the NylC Asp306 proposal. Exploratory QM/MM optimizations transferred that proton to Asp274, motivating a matched ASH274 WT MD follow-up. This is an observed model relaxation, not a pKa population assignment or proof that Nyl12 Asp274 is protonated.

slides.title: Static pKa estimates do not resolve protonation
slides.caption: PROPKA structure/chain ranges; MCCE is quantitatively unqualified.
slides.notes: These are default PROPKA estimates across retained structure/chain preparations; ranges are observed across structures/chains, not confidence intervals. Nyl12 primary site E includes three static geometries: Asp272 0.88–2.37, Asp274 3.44–6.95, Thr233 Nα 8.93–9.70. Mature NylC 5XYG default estimates are Asp306 2.19–2.21, Asp308 5.49–6.49, and Thr267 N 6.35–6.55. Uncleaved precursor structures 7YU0 and 7YU1 contain mutations; they were not back-mutated, so cleavage and mutation effects are confounded. The Thr N terminus is not free in these uncleaved structures. Coupled-state alternatives vary substantially and are not a unique assignment. MCCE quality checks are incomplete; its values are not interpreted. A ~3.91 Å nearest Asp O–O separation is discussed in the NylC mechanism notes, not mixed into this pKa table. Latest20November complete-Nyl12 MCCE diagnostic finished but curves were mostly saturated overpH0–14; Asp272 sigmoid fit disagreed with midpoint, His257 label contradicted curve, and FTPL/legacy proline parameters differed. No quantitative catalytic MCCE pKa accepted. Matched HIS-normalized snapshot PROPKA acrosssites: ThrN7.06–9.70,Asp2721.02–1.99,Asp2742.95–4.37. These are different conformer/protonation preparations from the3snapshot primary-siteE ranges tabulated here; do not pool them as uncertainty intervals. No automatic protonation-state assignment follows.

slides.title: Asp274 protonation did not improve WT geometry
slides.caption: Four independent trajectories per state; bars = mean, error bars = sample SD.
slides.notes: The plotted observable is the fraction of frames meeting either the stringent or broader defined attack/oxyanion-hole geometry set. Means ± between-replica SD: NH2/ASP272/ASP274 27.77 ± 24.64%; NH2/ASP272/ASH274 5.18 ± 6.80%; NH3+/ASP272/ASP274 28.99 ± 12.99%. Native-Thr occupancy is 0.0175%, 0.245%, and 0%, respectively. These are correlated structural observations from four replicas, not activity, rate, or protonation population. The ASH274 state did not improve occupancy under this matched protocol. Matched four100ns replicas per state; neutral Thr Nα with ASP272/ASP274, neutral Nα with ASP272/ASH274, and protonated Nα with ASP272/ASP274. These fixed-charge occupancies do not establish equilibrium protonation populations. PROPKA is structure-dependent; MCCE validation incomplete. Negoro2023 AspCOOH inference is circumstantial and precursor mutagenesis confounds maturation with mature hydrolysis. Audit: scientific_acceptance.json specifies12 matched replicas,4 per state. occupancy_by_replica.csv independently lists12 cases (__replica_01..04 per state), each10000 analyzed frames; four enzyme copies are not treated as four independent trajectories.

No molecular image is used here; the active-site context render is not the exact QM subsystem. Native QM membership from model/inputs/dimer.mdin and system.prmtop: Ile112 partial segment (17 atoms, no backbone N); Phe113 partial segment (18 atoms, N/H/CA plus side chain, no C/O); Asn186 side chain (8); full Thr233 (15); partial Thr234 segment (12, no C/O); Asp272 and Asp274 side chains (6 each); and two local PA6 amide fragments (8 atoms each). slides.title: Fixed-geometry benchmarks support cautious DFTB3 use
slides.caption: ¹ kcal mol⁻¹; reference ωB97X-D/def2-SVP. Fixed-geometry comparisons.
slides.notes: The coupled-path panel compares six fixed geometries with ωB97X-D/def2-SVP; DFTB3 relative-profile RMSE is 3.27 kcal/mol and error reaches +7.42 kcal/mol for the TI1-like structure. Point-charge membership varied across windows (8104–7999), so this is a finite-embedding method diagnostic, not a validated reaction-energy profile; a fixed-membership check remains. A separate five-window matched electrostatic-embedding benchmark tests Thr233 OH→Nα proton transfer (not direct transfer to substrate amide N): DFTB3 RMSE 1.49 kcal/mol, endpoint error −0.57; GFN2-xTB RMSE 3.91, endpoint +7.93. Neither fixed-geometry comparison establishes gradients, a stationary point, a barrier, or a PMF.

slides.title: MD precedes MM and QM/MM structural refinement
slides.notes: The workflow begins from equilibrated enzyme–substrate (E–S) snapshots sampled under explicit protonation states. Validate atom mapping, proton inventory, covalent connectivity and QM/MM membership before minimization. MM minimization removes local strain in the chosen classical model. DFTB3/MM minimization then treats the reactive center quantum mechanically. These steps refine starting structures; they do not guarantee every snapshot is catalytically competent or prove a stable intermediate. Reactive TI1/acyl states are not accepted using the PA6 classical force field alone.

slides.title: Two acylation proposals differ in proton transfer
slides.caption: A: Thr233 OH → amide N; B: OH → Nα → amide N. TI1: tetrahedral intermediate.
slides.notes: Mechanism A transfers the Thr233 side-chain hydroxyl proton directly to the scissile substrate amide nitrogen as Thr233 OG1 attacks the substrate carbonyl. Mechanism B relays that proton first to the Thr233 N-terminal α-amino group (Nα), then from Nα to the substrate amide nitrogen during acylation. These are distinct hypotheses. Similar E–S endpoints or product composition do not establish a shared frozen reference, Hamiltonian, sampling coordinate, or comparable free-energy profile.

slides.title: Mechanism A has a high potential-energy maximum
slides.caption: Mechanism A potential-energy path; the highest band image is not a verified transition state.
slides.notes: This canonical band contains the direct Thr233 OG1–H to scissile substrate amide-N route (Mechanism A), with DFTB3/MM energies. The maximum is about 35.81 kcal/mol relative to the stated E–S reference. The band is converged as a NEB path, but the highest image has not been verified as an index-1 transition state with a downhill connection. Treat the plotted value as a potential-energy profile (PES) maximum, not ΔG‡. It is not directly comparable with the N-terminal-relay PES without common Hamiltonian/reference/coordinate analysis.

slides.title: Direct-seeded sampling mixes proton-transfer channels
slides.caption: q_acyl is the projected acylation coordinate; this mixed-channel marginal is unconverged.
slides.notes: The latest 22 November 2026 retained q_acyl marginal is about 47.05 kcal/mol for direct-seeded umbrella sampling. The 63-window dataset includes configurations with competing proton-transfer channels, including N-terminal-relay-like frames, so this is not a route-pure Mechanism A PMF. Target effective sample size was about 7.29, with drift flags in windows 028/030/032. It is preliminary and unconverged. Its q_acyl projection/reference differs from the three-coordinate arclength profile used for Mechanism B, so the maxima must not be directly subtracted.

slides.title: An addition-like structure motivates relay acylation
slides.caption: Bias-free optimization; full minimum curvature and lifetime remain unverified.
slides.notes: The w033 internal candidate came from direct-seeded umbrella MD, which also sampled N-terminal-relay configurations; umbrella bias was then removed before QM/MM optimization. This lineage explains how an addition-like relay structure emerged from a direct-seeded campaign. It retained partial tetrahedral character with C–OG1=1.740 Å, C–N=1.490 Å, C–O=1.309 Å; gradient was 7.94×10⁻⁶ Eh/bohr. Label it addition-like or TI1-like, not a proven stable TI1 minimum. Full Hessian/minimum curvature and an unbiased lifetime are not established. This active-site rendering contains 152 local atoms and provides context only; it is not a visualization of the exact 98-real-atom QM subsystem. E–S/acyl endpoints may share chemical composition but not automatically a common frozen environment/reference.
